definition: Guile means the use of cunning deceit to gain an advantage.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word guile. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know guile should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The campaign was won by guile: her team leaked a false itinerary, and the rival candidate spent the final week shadowing an empty bus.
Shrewdness is milder than guile — shrewdness reads the game sharply but still plays it straight.
Treachery goes further than guile: guile outwits strangers and rivals, while treachery betrays the very people who trusted you.

Craftiness is the everyday name for the talent guile names — getting your way by sly, tricky dealing. Guile is the more literary word, and it suggests the deceit is elegant, almost admirable in its skill; craftiness is homelier, as small as a card-table bluff.

Artifice is clever contrivance — a trick built, not a lie told: a false itinerary, a staged tour, a prop with a job to do. Guile is the standing talent behind such devices; artifice names one constructed trick. A schemer has guile; the scheme shows artifice.

When the cleverness is honest, the fair words are finesse or shrewdness.

At forty-one, Ilona Vasquez gave away twenty years and a foot of reach to every opponent on the veterans' tour.
She won anyway, and the how of it was the tour's favorite subject.

Her matches ran on guile: a serve that looked identical whether it curved wide or straight, a slow ball disguised as a hard one until the last half-second, an exhausted slump between points that vanished the instant the ball was live.
Younger players studied the film and swore nothing she did was illegal; nothing was.
She simply made you certain of the wrong thing, point after point, until the set was gone.
